# Workshop goal

This vignette introduces the BirdFlow workflows involving population-level migration phenology inference.

-   Our main goal is to use synthetic BirdFlow routes to estimate the timing of immigration into and emigration from a selected geographic region.

The vignette also includes several optional extensions for more advanced applications.

-   Extension 1 compares migration phenology between two regions.
-   Extension 2 allows participants to choose their own species and region.

# Workflow

``` text
BirdFlow synthetic routes
        |
        v
For each route and date:
Is the bird inside the selected region?
        |
        v
Compare consecutive timesteps
        |
        +--> Immigration:
        |    outside at previous timestep
        |    -> inside at current timestep
        |
        +--> Emigration:
             inside at previous timestep
             -> outside at current timestep
        |
        v
Count events across simulated routes
        |
        v
Divide by total number of simulated routes
        |
        v
Regional immigration and emigration phenology
```

# Installation

```{r install-packages, eval=TRUE}
cran_packages <- c(
  "remotes",
  "dplyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "sf",
  "terra",
  "scales",
  "RColorBrewer",
  "patchwork",
  "cowplot",
  "tibble",
  "rmarkdown",
  "knitr"
)

missing_cran <- cran_packages[!cran_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())]

if (length(missing_cran) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_cran, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}

if (!requireNamespace("BirdFlowR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  remotes::install_github("birdflow-science/BirdFlowR")
}
```

```{r load-packages}
library(dplyr)

}
```

```{r load-model}
BirdFlowR::birdflow_options(cache = file.path(getwd(), "downloaded_models"))

  timeout=120
)
bf

```

```{r example-season-dates}

bf$dates #lookup_date

```

```{r inspect-season-dates}
prebreeding_dates <- get_season_dates(bf, season = "prebreeding")
```

# Define a rectangular region of interest

This first workflow uses a simple geographic box.

```{r define-box}
region <- list(
  name = "Baltimore Oriole demonstration region",
  lon_min = -92.548990,
  lon_max = -86.004801,
  lat_min = 37.411889,
  lat_max = 40.613238
)

region
```

# Visualize synthetic routes and the region

```{r route-map}
# Extract routes
routes <- BirdFlowR::route(
  bf,
  n = 200,
  season = "prebreeding"
)

# Turn the box into sfc format
bbox_geo <- sf::st_as_sfc(
  sf::st_bbox(
    c(
      xmin = region$lon_min,
      xmax = region$lon_max,
      ymin = region$lat_min,
      ymax = region$lat_max
    ),
    crs = 4326
  )
)

# Project the box to the BirdFlow coordinates
map_crs <- sf::st_crs(terra::crs(bf$geom$crs))

bbox_projected <- sf::st_transform(
  bbox_geo,
  crs = map_crs
)

# Plot the routes and boxes
p_routes <- plot(routes) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    data = bbox_projected,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = NA,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = region$name)

p_routes

```

# Regional abundance through spring

Before using simulated routes to infer movement into and out of the region, we can first examine how abundance within the region changes through the spring.

```{r spring-regional-abundance}
spring_abundance <- calculate_regional_abundance(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = region$lon_min,
  lon_max = region$lon_max,
  lat_min = region$lat_min,
  lat_max = region$lat_max,
  season = "prebreeding"
)

spring_abundance
```

```{r spring-regional-abundance-plot}
p_spring_abundance <- plot_regional_abundance(
  regional_abundance = spring_abundance,
  title = "Spring abundance within the selected region"
)

p_spring_abundance
```

The abundance curve shows when the modeled population increases and decreases within the region. However, abundance alone does not tell us how birds are moving across the region boundary. For example, an increase in abundance could reflect strong immigration, low emigration, or both. To separate these processes, we use BirdFlow synthetic routes to track movement into and out of the region.

# Spring phenology

```{r spring-simulation}
spring_case <- run_phenology_case_study(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = region$lon_min,
  lon_max = region$lon_max,
  lat_min = region$lat_min,
  lat_max = region$lat_max,
  season = "prebreeding",
  n_routes = params$n_routes,
  filter_tracks = FALSE
)

# Simulate weekly enter-leave pattern (important)
spring_weekly <- spring_case$weekly_movement

head(spring_weekly)

```

Columns:

-   date: Calendar date represented by the BirdFlow timestep.
-   n_enters: Number of simulated routes that enter the region between consecutive timesteps.
-   n_leaves: Number of simulated routes that leave the region between consecutive timesteps.
-   date_mid: Date converted to POSIXct for smoothing and plotting.
-   enters_scaled: Number entering divided by the total number of simulated routes.
-   leaves_scaled: Number leaving divided by the total number of simulated routes.

## Spring immigration and emigration

```{r spring-movement-plot}
p_spring_movement <- plot_immigration_emigration(
  weekly_route_changes = spring_weekly,
  title = "Spring immigration and emigration"
)

p_spring_movement
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
spring_xlim <- range(spring_abundance$date, na.rm = TRUE)

p_spring_movement_aligned <- p_spring_movement +
  ggplot2::scale_x_datetime(
    limits = as.POSIXct(spring_xlim),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

p_spring_abundance_aligned <- p_spring_abundance +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    limits = spring_xlim,
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  )

extension_1_plot <-
  p_spring_movement_aligned /
  p_spring_abundance_aligned +
  patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1))

extension_1_plot
```

## How route-based phenology is calculated

The code turns simulated BirdFlow routes into a weekly summary of movement into and out of the selected region.

``` text
BirdFlow synthetic routes
        |
        v
For each route and date:
Is the bird inside the selected region?
        |
        v
Compare consecutive timesteps
        |
        +--> Immigration:
        |    outside at previous timestep
        |    -> inside at current timestep
        |
        +--> Emigration:
             inside at previous timestep
             -> outside at current timestep
        |
        v
Count events across simulated routes
        |
        v
Divide by total number of simulated routes
        |
        v
Regional immigration and emigration phenology
```

## A small under-the-hood example

The helper function above does several data-wrangling steps. The basic idea is easier to see with a tiny example.

Imagine we simulated three BirdFlow routes across four dates. For each route and date, we first ask whether the bird is inside the selected region.

```{r under-hood-example-data}
toy_route_days <- tibble::tribble(
  ~route_id, ~date,          ~inside,
  1,         "2026-04-01",   FALSE,
  1,         "2026-04-08",   TRUE,
  1,         "2026-04-15",   TRUE,
  1,         "2026-04-22",   TRUE,

  2,         "2026-04-01",   FALSE,
  2,         "2026-04-08",   FALSE,
  2,         "2026-04-15",   TRUE,
  2,         "2026-04-22",   FALSE,

  3,         "2026-04-01",   TRUE,
  3,         "2026-04-08",   TRUE,
  3,         "2026-04-15",   FALSE,
  3,         "2026-04-22",   FALSE
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(date = as.Date(date))

toy_route_days
```

For each route, we compare the current inside/outside status with the previous and next date. A route enters when it was outside before but is inside now. A route leaves when it is inside before but outside now.

```{r under-hood-entry-exit}
toy_route_changes <- toy_route_days |>
  dplyr::arrange(route_id, date) |>
  dplyr::group_by(route_id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    prev_inside = dplyr::lag(
      inside,
      default = dplyr::first(inside)
    ),
    inside = inside,
    enters = !prev_inside & inside,
    leaves = prev_inside & !inside
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::relocate(
    route_id, date, prev_inside, inside, enters, leaves
  )

toy_route_changes
```

Finally, we summarize these route-level changes by date. This gives the weekly immigration curve, emigration curve.

```{r under-hood-weekly-summary}
toy_weekly_summary <- toy_route_changes |>
  dplyr::group_by(date) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_enters = sum(enters),
    n_leaves = sum(leaves),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

toy_weekly_summary
```

Because the number of simulated routes is arbitrary, we usually divide these counts by the total number of routes. This turns the values into proportions of simulated routes (proportion of population).

```{r under-hood-scaled-summary}
n_toy_routes <- dplyr::n_distinct(toy_route_changes$route_id)

toy_weekly_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    enters_scaled = n_enters / n_toy_routes,
    leaves_scaled = n_leaves / n_toy_routes
  )
```

In the full workflow, the same logic is applied to thousands of simulated BirdFlow routes. The curves in the plots are smoothed versions of these weekly summaries.

# Fall phenology

```{r fall-simulation}
fall_case <- run_phenology_case_study(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = region$lon_min,
  lon_max = region$lon_max,
  lat_min = region$lat_min,
  lat_max = region$lat_max,
  season = "postbreeding",
  n_routes = params$n_routes,
  filter_tracks = FALSE
)

fall_weekly <- fall_case$weekly_movement
head(fall_weekly)
```

## Fall immigration and emigration

```{r fall-movement-plot}
p_fall_movement <- plot_immigration_emigration(
  weekly_route_changes = fall_weekly,

)

p_fall_movement
```

# Combined phenology figure

```{r combined-phenology-figure, fig.width=17, fig.height=8}
# Combined phenology figure
movement_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(
  p_spring_movement +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.box = "horizontal"
    )
)

p_spring_clean <- p_spring_movement +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

p_fall_clean <- p_fall_movement +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )

right_panel <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_spring_clean,
  p_fall_clean,
  movement_legend,
  ncol = 1,
  rel_heights = c(1, 1, 0.15)
)

combined_phenology_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_routes,
  right_panel,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1, 1)
)

combined_phenology_plot
```

# Extension 1: compare two rectangular regions

In this extension, we compare the phenology of two regions with different latitude.

```{r compare-two-regions, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
region_a <- list(
  name = "Southern region",
  lon_min = -90,
  lon_max = -80,
  lat_min = 30,
  lat_max = 36
)

region_b <- list(
  name = "Northern region",
  lon_min = -90,
  lon_max = -80,
  lat_min = 42,
  lat_max = 48
)

make_region_rect <- function(region) {
  sf::st_as_sfc(
    sf::st_bbox(
      c(
        xmin = region$lon_min,
        xmax = region$lon_max,
        ymin = region$lat_min,
        ymax = region$lat_max
      ),
      crs = 4326
    )
  ) |>
    sf::st_sf(region = region$name, geometry = _)
}

region_rects <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_region_rect(region_a),
  make_region_rect(region_b)
)

region_rects_projected <- sf::st_transform(
  region_rects,
  crs = sf::st_crs(terra::crs(bf$geom$crs))
)

comparison_routes <- BirdFlowR::route(
  bf,
  n = 300,
  season = "prebreeding"
)

p_regions <- plot(comparison_routes) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    data = region_rects_projected,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = NA,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

case_a <- run_phenology_case_study(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = region_a$lon_min,
  lon_max = region_a$lon_max,
  lat_min = region_a$lat_min,
  lat_max = region_a$lat_max,
  season = "prebreeding",
  n_routes = 2000,
  filter_tracks = FALSE
)

case_b <- run_phenology_case_study(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = region_b$lon_min,
  lon_max = region_b$lon_max,
  lat_min = region_b$lat_min,
  lat_max = region_b$lat_max,
  season = "prebreeding",
  n_routes = 2000,
  filter_tracks = FALSE
)

p_a <- plot_immigration_emigration(
  weekly_route_changes = case_a$weekly_movement,
  title = region_a$name
) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14)
  )

p_b <- plot_immigration_emigration(
  weekly_route_changes = case_b$weekly_movement,
  title = region_b$name
) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14)
  )

extension_1_plot <-
  p_regions +
  (p_b/ p_a) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2, 2.2))

extension_1_plot
```

# Extension 2: Participant activity -- pick your own species

Choose one species model from the BirdFlow 2026 model collection:

```{r participant-link}
params$model_collection_page
```

Then choose a region of interest.

For example, you might choose:

1.  A breeding region.
2.  A migration stopover region.
3.  A state or county.
4.  A region where you have field data.
5.  A region where you expect early or late arrival.

To find the longitudes and latitudes of a geographic box, you can use this website:

[https://bboxfinder.com/](https://bboxfinder.com/#40.178873,-92.153320,43.197167,-85.385742)

or <https://boundingbox.klokantech.com>

Edit these values and rerun the vignette:

```{r participant-template}
my_model_url <- "https://birdflow-science.s3.amazonaws.com/2026/camwar_best_dg.hdf5"
my_model_name <- "camwar_best_dg"

my_region <- list(
  name = "My study region",
  lon_min = -92.153320,
  lon_max = -85.385742,
  lat_min = 40.178873,
  lat_max = 43.197167
)

BirdFlowR::birdflow_options(cache = file.path(getwd(), "downloaded_models"))
bf <- BirdFlowR::load_model(
  my_model_name, 
  collection_url = params$model_collection_base, 
  timeout=120
)

spring_case <- run_phenology_case_study(
  bf = bf,
  lon_min = my_region$lon_min,
  lon_max = my_region$lon_max,
  lat_min = my_region$lat_min,
  lat_max = my_region$lat_max,
  season = "prebreeding",
  n_routes = params$n_routes,
  filter_tracks = FALSE
)

spring_weekly <- spring_case$weekly_movement
p_spring_movement <- plot_immigration_emigration(
  weekly_route_changes = spring_weekly,
  title = "Spring movement decomposition"
)

p_spring_movement

```
